items.title: 61427_Happy Caldwell oral history interview
items.q: Horace just treated Fletcher so bad when he came here.

ctx.x: But I mean what you were saying about Horace was --

Horace just treated Fletcher so bad when he came here. He brought a little group here from out of -- from out of Ohio. And Fletcher, you know, he was a good piano player, and Fletcher would loan him his car, would run off with Fletcher's car, and he stole a lot of themusic and all like that. And the saddest thing of it was, after Fletcher had passed, they had Fletcher's funeral down at Mother AME Zion Church on 137th Street and 7th Avenue, one of the oldest Negro churches in the state of New York City because…

And we were looking for Horace. Didn't show up. So John Hammond said 'Hop, can you see Horace? I say, well, this is funny. (unintelligible). I'm looking to see if I can see him, but he wasn't there. Nobody see him.
